title: Relative affine criterion for fpqc sheaves
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and F a set-valued presheaf on schemes over S. Suppose F is an fppf sheaf [def-pc-fppf-site]. If F satisfies the sheaf condition for every singleton Spec A -> Spec R induced by a flat surjective spectrum map, for each structure map Spec R -> S, then F is an fpqc sheaf on Over S [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. The value universe is the scheme universe; no finiteness or nonemptiness condition is imposed on covering families.

proof.text: Form H(T) as pairs (s:T->S,x in F(T,s)); its restriction sends (s,x) to (s composed with the test map,the restriction of x). The functor laws follow from the functor laws of F and associativity.

For any covering family, first glue the structure maps to S by representable descent, then glue the sections on the resulting fixed S-scheme by the relative sheaf condition. Conversely, a gluing of pairs over a fixed S-scheme has the prescribed structure map by representable uniqueness. These arguments give the two explicit relative/absolute sheaf-condition implications, including empty families.

The fppf sheaf assumption gives Zariski descent of H. The affine singleton assumption gives the affine condition of the absolute fpqc criterion for H. Apply that criterion, then the reverse implication of the previous step to obtain fpqc descent for F.
